PRP Opening Note 11/19
Anthropic prices the largest IPO on record at $83. Twenty-two banks share the spoils. Credit desks feel the strain. Rogue AI as the most underpriced risk
 
Anthropic prices the largest IPO on record at $83 Above its $70-to-$78 range, upsizing the offering and including the $26 billion private placement, The price values the company at about $1.5 trillion. Gray-market trading points to a pop of 20% or more at the open. A strong first day reopens the door for the 2027 tech IPO queue and the ECM teams waiting on it. (Bloomberg, Reuters).
Twenty-two banks share the spoils - Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead a 22-bank syndicate, including JPMorgan, Citi, Bank of America and Jefferies. Before the price was raised, Evercore ISI's Glenn Schorr estimated total underwriting fees at roughly $395 million. One deal this size can change how a bank's ECM bonus pool looks this year (Bloomberg, FourWeekMBA)..
Ex-junior bankers' AI startup Rogo nears a $3.75 billion valuation Rogo, founded by former Lazard banker Gabriel Stengel and JPMorgan alumnus John Willett, is said to be raising about $350 million, up from a $2 billion valuation in April. Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and JPMorgan use it, and Citi rolled the tool out in the U.S. and UK last week. Wider use of AI modeling tools is changing how banks staff and train analysts. Banks are rethinking what they need from first-year analysts. (Bloomberg).
Credit desks feel the strain. Lenders describe debt repricing across markets at once as a "a real fear factor". Hedge funds are nursing losses on low-rated debt. Restructuring and liability-management bankers should stay busy into 2027. Weaker borrowers facing higher rates means more restructuring and liability-management work.
Rogue AI as the most underpriced risk A frontier AI model breaking out of its sandbox and damaging part of the economy is the risk markets are pricing least. It is a notable warning from inside one of the two banks leading Anthropic's IPO. Bloomberg
 
One record deal can lift an ECM bonus pool, but the analyst seat keeps changing. How is your team adjusting junior roles?

text.text:
With all these major technology outages lately, I'm starting to wonder if I should be checking the news or checking my generator and toilet paper inventory!

Between the FAA grounding flights, disruptions involving Microsoft, Bank of America, Apple, and reports of problems at the NSA, it seems like every time you turn around, something else is going down!

And apparently, people are getting nervous enough that they're heading to Costco to stock up on emergency supplies.

Does anybody else remember COVID?

You couldn't find toilet paper, paper towels, or bottled water anywhere!
I'm still not sure why toilet paper becomes the most valuable commodity in America whenever there's a crisis, but apparently, it's right up there with gold!

Now, I don't know whether these recent outages are connected, and there's no established evidence that they are. Officials have attributed various disruptions to technical problems rather than coordinated attacks.

But with AI advancing at an incredible pace and all the talk about superintelligence, I do wonder how prepared we are for something more serious.

And I say that as somebody who's always taken preparedness pretty seriously.
I'm an Eagle Scout, and our motto was simple: Be Prepared.

Apparently, I took that motto a little more seriously than some of my fellow Scouts!
I've got a generator, solar power, batteries, plenty of food and water, and other emergency supplies.

Of course, living in Texas, there are always a few folks who think the answer to every emergency is having 10,000 rounds of ammunition!

I'm all for protecting yourself and your family, but you can't eat bullets, and they won't keep your refrigerator running!

All joking aside, these disruptions do concern me.
Our government, banking systems, airlines, businesses, and practically everything else depend on technology working properly.

What happens if the next major outage affects the electrical grid?
Or our water treatment plants and water distribution systems?
And what if something that normally takes a few hours to fix takes several days or even weeks?

Living in Texas, we've already experienced what happens when the electrical grid has serious problems. It's not much fun!

I'm certainly not predicting some catastrophic event, and I hope these recent incidents are nothing more than unrelated technical failures.

But I do wonder whether we're becoming so dependent on technology that we're not adequately prepared when it fails.

I'd really like to hear what everybody thinks.
Are these outages simply an unfortunate coincidence, or are they warning signs that our infrastructure is becoming increasingly vulnerable?

Do you think AI will make these systems safer and more reliable, or introduce even more risks? And are you personally prepared if the power, internet, or water goes out for an extended period?

I'm genuinely curious what people think about all this.

In the meantime, I'm going to make sure my generator starts, my batteries are charged, and I've got plenty of toilet paper!

#Technology #Cybersecurity #Infrastructure #ArtificialIntelligence #BePrepared

text.text:
The "AI Dollar" Has Arrived—And Its Direction Is Still Unclear

In a compelling new piece for Reuters, Mike Dolan breaks down how artificial intelligence and semiconductors are reshaping the U.S. dollar and global capital flows:

AI as a growth engine: Massive investments in data centers, chips, and AI infrastructure have helped power U.S. GDP growth—driving the dollar index (.DXY) to 19-month highs on expectations of a firmer Fed stance.
"Chipdollars" vs. Treasuries: As Deutsche Bank notes, global chip trade has surpassed oil and gas, with cross-border surpluses flowing more into U.S. equities than traditional safe-haven Treasuries—bringing higher market volatility.
A tug-of-war ahead: While hyperscaler capex plans remain resilient for now, Bank of America's fund manager survey highlights growing caution around tech concentration and spending discipline, leaving the dollar's trajectory open as we head toward 2027.
A must-read for anyone tracking where macro liquidity, tech valuations, and real-economy fundamentals are heading next.
